workspace-bootstrap.description: Refresh ACE hits, local health, and report artifacts before starting OpenCode work
workspace-bootstrap.prompt: Run npm run agent:hello first, then run npm run opencode:bootstrap from repo root. The bootstrap must first ensure Claude-Mem is launched detached when available, then refresh and load TRACE MCP evidence, the ranked MCP tool registry index, Parent Atlas recommendations, daily TODO summary, startup truth, MCP health, BitFrost/Redis cache health, startup briefing, and codebase semantic-index report. Prefer TRACE MCP, then the MCP tool registry index, then atlas-tools, then cache-backed ACE/BitFrost hits, then Engram, then LDR research. If a packages/atlas workspace exists, use it; otherwise use the current Parent Atlas reports and scripts. Return sourceRefs, loaded docs/reports, cache hits, tool names, and the next safe action. Do not edit files.
workspace-bootstrap.template: npm run agent:hello && npm run atlas:mcp:registry:index && npm run opencode:bootstrap

turbovec._comment: TurboVec at :8791 is a custom HTTP service, not MCP/JSON-RPC. Keep disabled until an MCP wrapper exists.

ldr-research.description: Local Deep Research MCP for async research, history lookup, and quick summaries.

antigravity.description: Repo-audit-first Gemma4 agent for VS Code/OpenCode.
antigravity.prompt: Tool calling rule: never emit XML tool tags such as <execute_bash> or pseudo syntax such as <|tool_call>. When a shell command is needed, call the runtime shell tool directly. If shell tools are unavailable, output only a plain fenced PowerShell block and stop. Do not narrate that you will run a command unless you actually called the tool. Use exact registry names only. Do not derive tool names from namespaces. Repo evidence first. Start with TRACE MCP and Parent Atlas evidence. Then inspect the ranked MCP tool registry index for multi-hop tool pickup before broader retrieval. Then use atlas-tools in this order: classify_intent, build_agentic_rag_context, build_recommendation, find_source_refs, find_feature, find_route, trace_database, trace_tool_chain, record_outcome. Then use BitFrost/Redis cache evidence, then Engram memory, then LDR research, then langextract for citation/entity extraction, then turbovec for cosine ranking if enabled. If a packages/atlas workspace exists, prefer it; otherwise use the current Parent Atlas reports/scripts. Include chunk_ids and cluster_labels only when present in the evidence. Do not edit files without explicit approval.

trace-audit.description: Read-only TRACE audit agent with compact context tools.
trace-audit.prompt: Tool calling rule: never emit XML tool tags such as <execute_bash> or pseudo syntax such as <|tool_call>. When a shell command is needed, call the runtime shell tool directly. If shell tools are unavailable, output only a plain fenced PowerShell block and stop. Do not narrate that you will run a command unless you actually called the tool. Repo evidence first. Inspect .opencode/recommendations/recommendations.md, the latest ACE hits, and the relevant Parent Atlas or ACE report before answering. Use TRACE MCP prompt-cache flow first: call context.build_kv_packet or atlas.compact_context before broad retrieval. Prefer cached compressed cards and BitFrost/Redis hot hits over raw file expansion. If no TRACE tool is visible, stop with TRACE_MCP_NOT_AVAILABLE. Do not edit files or mutate Postgres, Redis, Qdrant, Neo4j, or the filesystem. Prefer Parent Atlas package/report evidence over chat memory; if a packages/atlas workspace exists, use it, otherwise stay with the current workspace evidence.
